items.title: Finite statistical microstate model
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
A finite statistical microstate model is a pair $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ where $\Omega$ is a finite nonempty set and $\epsilon:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ assigns a finite numerical energy to each microstate. The physical energy of $x\in\Omega$ is $E(x)=\epsilon(x)\,\mathrm J$, with its zero and any retained internal offsets fixed by the declared material model. For a physical internal-energy interpretation, the declared companion mechanical model supplies, for every admitted microstate preparation $x$, a positive total mass and a center-of-mass position map with a defined componentwise velocity at that preparation, obeying the Galilean transformation conditions of [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. That velocity selects the statewise instantaneous rest chart in which $E(x)$ is recorded; a finite set and energy map alone do not construct these mechanical data or a common rest chart for a time interval. Bulk translational kinetic energy and separately tracked external-field energy are excluded from these internal-energy values. The energy zero and any internal offsets are fixed consistently across admitted states. If the statistical model also assigns a single equilibrium macrostate to a preparation, $U$ is its internal-energy coordinate of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]; the pair $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ alone does not assert that macroscopic identification. Equal energy values at distinct elements of $\Omega$ count as distinct microstates.

When two such models are declared independent, their joint microstate set is the Cartesian product $\Omega_A\times\Omega_B$, and additivity of the microscopic energy is the explicit condition $\epsilon_{AB}(x,y)=\epsilon_A(x)+\epsilon_B(y)$. Independence and this energy equation are model data; they do not follow merely from the two systems being separated. The definition itself assigns no weights, temperature, probability law, or dynamics.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.2–1.3 (printed pp. 2–27)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2–4.4 (printed pp. 192–208)

items.physical_scope: Finite discrete statistical models whose energies are numerical values in joules in the statewise instantaneous center-of-mass rest chart selected by separately supplied compatible mechanical data; no probability law or equilibration claim is part of the definition.

items.title: Regular Hamiltonian shell preparation data
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an integer $n\ge1$ and an open phase-coordinate domain $O_{\rm phys}\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ with physical canonical coordinates $q_i$ in metres and $p_i$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. The canonical symplectic form on this chart is $\omega_{\rm phys}=\sum_{i=1}^n dq_i\wedge dp_i$. Let $\hat q_i=q_i/(1\,\mathrm m)$ and $\hat p_i=p_i/(1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$, and let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ be the open image of the chart in these dimensionless coordinates. The corresponding dimensionless canonical form is $\hat\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n d\hat q_i\wedge d\hat p_i$, so $\omega_{\rm phys}=(1\,\mathrm{J\,s})\hat\omega$.

Let $\hat H:O\to\mathbb R$ be a numerical energy function with continuous partial derivatives through order two, and let $H_{\rm phys}:O_{\rm phys}\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ be $H_{\rm phys}(q,p)=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat H(\hat q,\hat p)$. Where defined, its physical Hamiltonian vector field $X_{H_{\rm phys}}$ is determined by $\iota_{X_{H_{\rm phys}}}\omega_{\rm phys}=dH_{\rm phys}$. For each elapsed time $t$ in its domain, the physical flow map is a function $\phi_t:D_t\to O_{\rm phys}$, where $D_t\subseteq O_{\rm phys}$ is the set of initial data whose trajectories exist through time $t$, and it satisfies $d\phi_t/dt=X_{H_{\rm phys}}\circ\phi_t$. Equivalently, in the dimensionless chart, the flow map $\hat\phi_{\hat t}:\hat D_{\hat t}\to O$ is generated by $X_{\hat H}$ satisfying $\iota_{X_{\hat H}}\hat\omega=d\hat H$, at dimensionless time $\hat t=t/(1\,\mathrm s)$; here $\hat D_{\hat t}$ is the set of initial coordinates whose trajectories exist through $\hat t$. These definitions specify the flow maps when they exist but impose no global-existence or completeness hypothesis on the shell preparation.

A specified open interval $J_E\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular compact-shell band when $\hat H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J_E$ and $\nabla\hat H$ is nonzero at every point of $\hat H^{-1}(J_E)$.

For $\hat E\in J_E$, the energy shell is $\Sigma_{\hat E}:=\{x\in O:\hat H(x)=\hat E\}$. The graph-chart definition of the weighted shell integral is [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]: in a local graph chart $x_i=h(z,\hat E)$, its coarea measure is $d\mu_{\hat E}=dA_{\hat E}/|\nabla\hat H|$, with graph-area factor and gradient in the dimensionless Euclidean coordinates. Set $D(\hat E):=\int_{\Sigma_{\hat E}}d\mu_{\hat E}$ and admit the preparation only when $\Sigma_{\hat E}\ne\varnothing$ and $0<D(\hat E)<\infty$. Its normalized shell law is $\nu_{\hat E}(A):=D(\hat E)^{-1}\mu_{\hat E}(A\cap\Sigma_{\hat E})$. The current draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]] proves the coarea identity, chart independence and positive finite shell mass under its stated $C^2$, compact-regular-band hypotheses; its statement and proof are present, while its acceptance remains unresolved. Multiplying the unnormalized shell measure by a fixed positive phase-volume normalization does not change $\nu_{\hat E}$.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.2 (printed pp. 2–16)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2–4.3 (printed pp. 192–204)

items.physical_scope: Declared finite-dimensional classical Hamiltonian models in one canonical phase chart, restricted to nonempty compact regular energy shells in the stated band; preparation uses the normalized coarea measure and does not require a globally complete flow, while flow invariance is a separate theorem.

items.title: Canonical sampling assumption for finite and normalized statistical models
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assign a positive temperature $T$ in kelvins and the exact framework constant $k_{\mathrm B}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ from [[def-td-si-quantities]], and put $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a finite microstate model $(\Omega,\epsilon)$, adopt the canonical preparation
$$P_\beta(x)=\frac{e^{-\beta E(x)}}{Z(\beta)},\qquad Z(\beta)=\sum_{x\in\Omega}e^{-\beta E(x)}.$$
Here $Z$ is dimensionless, positive, and finite because $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty.

The same adopted law may be assigned to a specified countable state model with its stated enumeration and energy list, or to a measurable model $(X,\Sigma,\mu,E)$ with a dimensionless reference measure $\mu$ and measurable energy $E:X\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$, only when $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$ for the declared series or integral. In those cases $P_\beta(i)=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z$ or the probability density is $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$ relative to $\mu$. The countable and integral conventions are those of [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]] and [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]] at their actual current draft statements.

This is an adopted statistical-mechanical preparation rule. It is not derived from the macroscopic thermodynamic laws, a finite bath, entropy maximization, or a time-evolution equation. It does not assert that a physical sample has this preparation; that identification is an additional model assumption to be tested against a specified preparation and apparatus.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3 (printed pp. 17–26)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4–4.6 (printed pp. 205–217)

items.physical_scope: Adopted canonical preparation assumptions for finite microstate models and explicitly declared countable or measurable energy models with a positive finite dimensionless partition function; the postulate asserts no dynamics, equilibration, or empirical validation.

items.title: Microcanonical sampling assumption
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
For the regular-shell branch below, assume AC as required by
[[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]] and its coarea-measure
supplier. No choice assumption is needed for the separate finite-window branch.

For a finite microstate model and a declared energy value $E_0$ in joules and resolution $\delta\ge0$ in joules, define the admitted window
$$\Omega_{E_0,\delta}:=\{x\in\Omega:|E(x)-E_0|\le\delta\}.$$
When this set is nonempty, adopt the uniform preparation $P(x)=|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|^{-1}$ on it and zero outside. Its dimensionless Boltzmann entropy is $\log|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|$, and its physical entropy convention is $k_{\mathrm B}\log|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. A zero-width window is allowed only when it contains at least one microstate.

For a continuous classical model, when the regular-band, nonempty-shell, and normalization hypotheses in [[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]] hold, the microcanonical preparation is the normalized shell measure $\nu_{\hat E}$ defined there. The shell preparation does not require a globally defined flow. These finite-window and regular-shell rules are adopted model preparations. They do not assert Hamiltonian ergodicity, equality with long-time averages, canonical sampling, or equilibration.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.2 (printed pp. 2–16)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §4.2 (printed pp. 192–198)

items.physical_scope: Adopted uniform weighting for a nonempty finite energy window or the normalized coarea law on an admitted regular compact Hamiltonian energy shell; neither rule is a consequence of dynamics or a claim about measured samples.

items.title: Countable canonical identities under a local moment envelope
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $I$ be a specified nonempty countable microstate list with energies $E_i$ in joules, counted once, and let $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ be open. For $\beta\in J_\beta$, define $Z(\beta)=\sum_i e^{-\beta E_i}$ and, when $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$, $p_i(\beta)=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z(\beta)$. Suppose every compact interval $K\subset J_\beta$ admits a summable sequence $a_i\ge0$ with $(1+|E_i|^2)e^{-\beta E_i}\le a_i$ for all $i$ and $\beta\in K$. Then $Z$ is $C^2$, $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\bar E_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$, and the dimensionless Gibbs entropy
$$s_\beta:=-\sum_i p_i\log p_i=\log Z+\beta\bar E_\beta$$
is finite. Define the physical Gibbs entropy by $S_\beta:=k_{\mathrm B}s_\beta$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Then $F_{\mathrm{stat}}:=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta$ for $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. A lower bound on the energies alone does not supply the summable envelope or finite partition function.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.1–1.3.4 (printed pp. 18–26)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2–4.4 (printed pp. 192–208)

items.physical_scope: Discrete countable energy lists with a specified enumeration and a uniform local summable second-moment envelope on an open positive inverse-temperature interval; no lower-energy-bound-only or arbitrary trace claim is made.

items.title: Energy-density concentration at differentiable lattice pressure
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
For the lattice model and canonical law of [[pthm-td-lattice-bulk-pressure]], let $p_L(\gamma)=L^{-d}\log Z_L(\gamma)$ converge pointwise on an open interval $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ to $p(\gamma)$. If $p$ is differentiable at $\beta\in J_\beta$, set $e=-p'(\beta)$ in joules per site. Then the canonical mean energy density satisfies $\mathbb E_{\beta,L}[H_L]/L^d\to e$, and for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $c>0$ and $L_0$ such that
$$\mathbb P_{\beta,L}\!\left(\left|H_L/L^d-e\right|\ge\varepsilon\right)\le2e^{-cL^d}\qquad(L\ge L_0).$$
The probability is the model's finite-volume canonical probability, not an observed frequency. No conclusion is asserted when $p$ is nondifferentiable.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.2 and 5.3.1 (printed pp. 19–20 and 156–157)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4.6 and 6.2.2 (printed pp. 207–208 and 330–333)

items.physical_scope: Conditional model probabilities for bounded finite-range lattice systems at a differentiability point of the limiting log-partition density; no concentration claim is made at a nondifferentiable point or for arbitrary observables.

items.title: Finite-bath canonical error under a smooth shell-entropy model
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume AC for the regular-shell reading of [[post-td-microcanonical-sampling]]. Let the subsystem have a finite nonempty state set $\Omega$ and internal energies $E_x$ in joules with $|E_x|\le L$, where $L$ is in joules. The bath model supplies an open interval $U$ containing $[u_0-L,u_0+L]$, with bath energies $u,u_0\in U$ in joules, and a dimensionless shell-log-weight function $s_B:U\to\mathbb R$; define the positive shell weight by $W_B(u):=e^{s_B(u)}$. Assume $s_B\in C^2(U)$ and $|s_B''(u)|\le M$ on the displayed interval, where $M$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-2}}$. The model adopts $\beta=s'_B(u_0)>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, $k_{\mathrm B}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and $T=(k_{\mathrm B}\beta)^{-1}$ in kelvins. Assume weak additive coupling and separately stipulate that microcanonical shell sampling induces subsystem weights $P_B(x)\propto W_B(u_0-E_x)=e^{s_B(u_0-E_x)}$; this induced-marginal rule is an additional bath-model assumption, not a consequence of the microcanonical sampling postulate alone. Let $P_C(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ be the corresponding canonical law. With $\delta=ML^2/2$ (dimensionless), the shell log-weight remainder obeys
$$|s_B(u_0-E_x)-s_B(u_0)+\beta E_x|\le\delta,$$
and the normalized laws satisfy
$$\sum_{x\in\Omega}|P_B(x)-P_C(x)|\le e^{2\delta}-1.$$
This is an $\ell^1$ probability-vector bound; it does not assert a universal error or a thermodynamic limit.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3 (printed pp. 17–20)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2 and 4.4 (printed pp. 192–198 and 205–208)

items.physical_scope: A finite subsystem weakly coupled additively to a bath whose dimensionless shell entropy is twice continuously differentiable with bounded curvature on the full exchanged-energy interval; this is a conditional model bound, not a universal finite-size estimate.

items.title: Finite canonical partition, energy, variance, entropy and free-energy identities
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ be a finite microstate model with energies $E_x=\epsilon(x)\,\mathrm J$ from [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]. Let $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$, and $P_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z(\beta)$ be the adopted preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]. With $\bar E_\beta=\sum_xP_\beta(x)E_x$, $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=\sum_xP_\beta(x)(E_x-\bar E_\beta)^2$, and $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_xP_\beta(x)\log P_\beta(x)$, the finite partition sum is positive and
$$-\partial_\beta\log Z=\bar E_\beta,\qquad \partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E),\qquad S_\beta=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\bar E_\beta).$$
Consequently the statistical free-energy value $F_{\mathrm{stat}}:=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ satisfies $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta$. The derivatives hold the finite state set and its energy list fixed. No equivalence with a macroscopic entropy or Helmholtz potential is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.1–1.3.4 (printed pp. 18–26)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4–4.6 (printed pp. 205–217)

items.physical_scope: Exact finite-sum predictions for the adopted canonical law on a fixed finite microstate list with fixed internal energies; the statistical free-energy value is not automatically identified with a macroscopic Legendre potential or an empirical thermodynamic measurement.

items.title: Canonical weights uniquely maximize finite-state entropy at their mean energy
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ be a finite nonempty microstate model, let $T>0$, and let $q_x=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ be its canonical probabilities at $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. Set $\bar E=\sum_xq_xE_x$. Among all probability vectors $r=(r_x)_{x\in\Omega}$ with $\sum_xr_x=1$ and $\sum_xr_xE_x=\bar E$, the dimensionless Shannon entropy
$$h(r):=-\sum_{x:r_x>0}r_x\log r_x$$
is uniquely maximized by $r=q$. The corresponding physical Gibbs entropy is $S(r):=k_{\mathrm B}h(r)$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and has the same unique maximizer. This is a finite-model variational theorem; it does not establish that a physical sample is prepared canonically.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3.3 (printed pp. 22–25)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §4.6.2 (printed pp. 216–217)

items.physical_scope: Finite probability distributions on the declared microstate set at a fixed positive temperature; the result is a conditional variational property of the model and does not derive the physical canonical-preparation postulate.

items.title: General quantum Gibbs normalization and canonical identities
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice and the canonical Gibbs-preparation assumption [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]. Restrict to its $G=H$ branch: the declared energy operator $H$ is self-adjoint, bounded below, and measured in joules; $T>0$ is in kelvins, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ has $0<Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta<\infty$. Suppose also that on an open interval $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ containing $\beta$, every compact $C\subset J_\beta$ admits a summable family $a_j\ge0$ with $(1+|E_j|^2)e^{-\gamma E_j}\le a_j$ for all energy eigenvalues $E_j$ and $\gamma\in C$. Let $(u_j)$ be the finite or countable complete orthonormal eigenfamily supplied by [[thm-tdmath-general-trace-gibbs-model]], repeated according to multiplicity, with $Hu_j=E_ju_j$, and put $\lambda_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_\beta$. The supplied trace identity gives $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, and these $\lambda_j$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho_\beta$. Define the spectral mean $\bar E_\beta:=\sum_j\lambda_jE_j$, the variance $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(H):=\sum_j\lambda_j(E_j-\bar E_\beta)^2$, the dimensionless entropy $s_\beta:=-\sum_j\lambda_j\log\lambda_j$, and the physical von Neumann entropy $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta):=k_{\mathrm B}s_\beta$. These are spectral-sum definitions for this commuting Gibbs density; no operator trace of an unbounded product is used. The supplied moment envelope makes these sums finite. Then
$$-\partial_\beta\log Z_\beta=\bar E_\beta,\qquad \partial_\beta^2\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(H),\qquad S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)=k_{\mathrm B}\bigl(\log Z_\beta+\beta\bar E_\beta\bigr).$$
Thus $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_\beta=\bar E_\beta-T S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)$. This statement does not extend the Helmholtz interpretation to an effective generator $H-\mu\mathcal N$.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.1–1.3.4 (printed pp. 18–26)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.3–4.4 (printed pp. 199–208)

items.physical_scope: A declared quantum model with a semibounded self-adjoint energy operator, trace-class Gibbs exponential, and local first-and-second-moment envelope; the result concerns the adopted Gibbs preparation and does not derive thermalization or a continuum spectrum.

items.title: Partition, Gibbs-entropy and free-energy factorization for independent finite systems
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement: Let two finite microstate models from [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]] have nonempty state sets $\Omega_A,\Omega_B$, energies $E_A,E_B$ in joules, and the same $T>0$. Assume their declared composite model has state set $\Omega_A\times\Omega_B$ and energy $E_{AB}(x,y)=E_A(x)+E_B(y)$, with no interaction term. Under the canonical sampling assumption [[post-td-canonical-sampling]], the partition function factorizes as $Z_{AB}=Z_AZ_B$, the joint canonical law is $P_{AB}=P_AP_B$, the Gibbs entropy satisfies $S_{AB}=S_A+S_B$, and the statistical free-energy value satisfies $F_{AB}=F_A+F_B$.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3.1 (printed pp. 18–19)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4.1 and 4.6 (printed pp. 205–217)

items.physical_scope: Finite composite models whose state set is explicitly the Cartesian product and whose microscopic energy is additive; no claim is made for interacting systems, interface terms, or experimental independence.

items.title: Invariance of a regular-shell microcanonical preparation
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let a physical Hamiltonian model satisfy [[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]] on a nonempty compact regular energy band, and adopt its normalized shell law by [[post-td-microcanonical-sampling]]. In addition to the definition's $C^2$ regularity, assume its numerical Hamiltonian $\hat H$ is $C^\infty$. Let $\phi_t$ be the physical Hamiltonian flow defined there, with $t$ measured in seconds, and assume it is an invertible smooth map of the whole band for every real time. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft mathematical interfaces [[thm-tdmath-hamiltonian-measure-and-recurrence]] and [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]], every shell probability $
u_{\hat E}$ is invariant:
$$
u_{\hat E}(\phi_t^{-1}(A))=
u_{\hat E}(A)$$
for every Borel set $A\subseteq\Sigma_{\hat E}$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$. This result asserts no ergodicity, time-average equality, or thermalization.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.2 (printed pp. 2–16)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §4.2 (printed pp. 192–198)

items.physical_scope: A classical Hamiltonian flow that is globally defined and invertible on a compact regular energy band with the stated coarea measure; invariance is not ergodicity, mixing, equilibration, or equality of time and ensemble averages.

items.title: Bulk log-partition pressure for a bounded finite-range lattice model
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Use the finite-alphabet, bounded, translation-invariant finite-range lattice model of [[def-tdmath-bounded-finite-range-lattice]], with physical interaction energies in joules, inverse temperature $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}>0$, and partition sum $Z_L(\beta)$. Suppose each site represents a fixed cell of volume $v_0>0$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$. Define the reduced log-partition density $p_L=L^{-d}\log Z_L$ and the lattice pressure convention $P_L=(k_{\mathrm B}T/v_0)p_L$ in pascals. Then $p_L$ and $P_L$ have finite limits as $L\to\infty$. If a second boundary-energy model on the same configuration sets differs pointwise by at most $C_bL^{d-1}$ joules for fixed $C_b$, it has the same limit.

The pressure convention in this statement is assigned to this lattice model. Equating it with a derivative-based macroscopic pressure or a measured mechanical pressure requires a separate model identification.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §5.3.1 (printed pp. 156–157)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §6.2.2 (printed pp. 330–333)

items.physical_scope: Finite-alphabet, bounded, translation-invariant finite-range interactions on free cubic lattices with a declared cell volume; the pressure convention is specific to this lattice model and implies no continuum-particle or long-range pressure law.

items.title: Measurable canonical identities for a dimensionless reference measure
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space with dimensionless reference measure, let $E:X\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ be a finite physical energy, and let $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ be an open inverse-temperature set in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. Set $E_*=1\,\mathrm J$, $e=E/E_*:X\to\mathbb R$, $b=E_*\beta$, and $J_b=E_*J_\beta$; measurability of $E$ means measurability of the dimensionless numerical coordinate $e$. Suppose $Z(\beta)=\int_Xe^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ is positive and finite on $J_\beta$, and for each compact $K\subset J_\beta$ there is an integrable $G_K\ge0$ with $(1+|e|^2)e^{-\beta E}=(1+|e|^2)e^{-be}\le G_K$ for every $\beta\in K$. Under the canonical sampling assumption [[post-td-canonical-sampling]], define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$, $\langle E\rangle_\beta=\int E p_\beta\,d\mu$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2$, $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$, and the relative Gibbs entropy is finite with $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta)$. Hence $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta$ for $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3–1.4 (printed pp. 18–30)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2–4.4 (printed pp. 192–208)

items.physical_scope: Measurable energy models with a dimensionless reference measure, positive finite partition integral, and compact-parameter local integrable second-moment envelope; no claim is made for an arbitrary phase-space measure or unbounded energy without these hypotheses.

items.title: Finite-sector quantum Gibbs preparation minimizes the declared free-energy functional
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Work in the nonzero finite-dimensional fixed-$N$ sector of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], with self-adjoint energy $H_N^\sigma$ in joules and assigned $T>0$ in kelvins. Adopt the Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] and its unit convention $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. For $F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-T S(\rho)$ over the declared sector density operators, the canonical preparation is the unique minimizer and
$$\min_\rho F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log\operatorname{tr}(e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}).$$
This quantum statistical functional is not identified here with a macroscopic Helmholtz potential without an additional model bridge; its minimum does not establish equilibration.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.3–1.3.4 (printed pp. 22–27)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4–4.6 (printed pp. 205–217)

items.physical_scope: The finite-dimensional fixed-particle-number quantum sector at assigned positive temperature, conditional on the adopted Gibbs-preparation assumption and the exact NRQM entropy/free-energy definitions; no equilibration or macroscopic thermodynamic-limit claim is made.

items.title: Finite bosonic and fermionic mode partition and occupation formulas
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice and adopt the quantum Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned temperature $T>0$ kelvins, with $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. A finite independent mode list means an integer $m\ge1$ and, for each $r\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$, a declared type B or F and an excitation energy $\varepsilon_r>0$ joules. For type B take the one-mode Fock Hilbert space with complete number basis $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N_0}$ and self-adjoint occupation operator $N_re_n=ne_n$ on its exact diagonal domain as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]]. For type F take $\mathcal H_r=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal basis $f_0,f_1$ and $N_rf_n=nf_n$. In either case put $H_r=\varepsilon_rN_r$, and write $u_{r,n}=e_n$ or $f_n$ according to the factor type. Define $\mathcal H^{(1)}=\mathcal H_1$ and recursively $\mathcal H^{(r+1)}=\mathcal H^{(r)}\widehat\otimes\mathcal H_{r+1}$ by the completed Hilbert tensor construction of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]; let $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^{(m)}$. The canonical orthonormal product basis is $u_{\mathbf n}=\bigotimes_r u_{r,n_r}$, indexed by $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_m)\in\mathcal C:=\prod_r\mathcal C_r$, where $\mathcal C_r=\mathbb N_0$ for type B and $\mathcal C_r=\{0,1\}$ for type F. If all factors are F then $\mathcal C$ is finite; otherwise it is countably infinite and is enumerated by increasing $\sum_r n_r$ and lexicographic order within each finite level, which is finite because every $n_r\le\sum_r n_r$. For each factor put $\hat\varepsilon_r=\varepsilon_r/(1\,\mathrm J)$. Define the numerical energy map $\hat E:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R$ by $\hat E(\mathbf n)=\sum_{r=1}^m\hat\varepsilon_rn_r$ and the physical energy $E(\mathbf n)=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat E(\mathbf n)$. Define the numerical self-adjoint diagonal operator $\hat H$ by $\hat Hu_{\mathbf n}=\hat E(\mathbf n)u_{\mathbf n}$ on the exact domain
$$D(\hat H)=\Bigl\{\psi\in\mathcal H:\sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathcal C}\hat E(\mathbf n)^2|\langle\psi,u_{\mathbf n}\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\};$$
when $\mathcal C$ is finite, $\hat H$ is a finite real diagonal endomorphism and is self-adjoint; when $\mathcal C$ is countably infinite, the diagonal-operator lemma [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]] gives $\hat H$ self-adjoint for the displayed enumeration. The physical total energy operator is $H=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat H$, with $Hu_{\mathbf n}=E(\mathbf n)u_{\mathbf n}$ and $D(H)=D(\hat H)$; multiplication by a nonzero real scalar preserves self-adjointness.
This sum-energy Hamiltonian with no interaction term is the definition of independence for this quantum model.

For one bosonic mode with excitation energy $\varepsilon>0$ joules, let $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ and let $N$ be its dimensionless occupation number. Its partition trace and mean occupation are
$$Z_B=(1-q)^{-1},\qquad \langle N\rangle_B=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}.$$
For a fermionic two-level occupation system with energies $0,\varepsilon$, the partition sum and excited-state occupation are
$$Z_F=1+q,\qquad \langle N\rangle_F=\frac{q}{1+q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}.$$
For a finite independent collection as defined above, write $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ and $Z=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta$. Then $0<Z<\infty$ and the joint occupation-basis law is $P_\beta(\mathbf n):=e^{-\beta E(\mathbf n)}/Z$. For each factor $r$, define its marginal law by $P_{\beta,r}(k):=\sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathcal C:\,n_r=k}P_\beta(\mathbf n)$. The trace satisfies $Z=\prod_{r=1}^m Z_r$, the joint law factorizes as $P_\beta(\mathbf n)=\prod_{r=1}^m(q_r^{n_r}/Z_r)$, and each marginal mean is the corresponding one-mode mean displayed above. These are exact model identities under the adopted preparation.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§3.5–3.6 (printed pp. 77–106)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§5.6–5.7 (printed pp. 277–303)

items.physical_scope: Declared finite lists of independent bosonic one-mode Fock systems or fermionic two-level occupation systems at assigned positive temperature; no interacting, infinite-mode, continuum, condensation, measured-occupation, or thermalization conclusion is asserted.

items.title: Cesaro dephasing for a discrete trace-class quantum model
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a self-adjoint quantum Hamiltonian bounded below with a complete discrete energy eigenfamily of finite multiplicity, and let $\rho_0$ be any positive trace-class density operator of trace one. Let $\hbar>0$ be the assigned action constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, adopt the unitary dynamics $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ of [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], and assume the trace-class Gibbs and local moment conditions of [[pthm-td-general-quantum-canonical-identities]] that supply this discrete eigenfamily. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing]], the Cesaro state
$$\bar\rho_\tau:=\frac1{\tau}\int_0^\tau U_t\rho_0U_t^*\,dt$$
converges in trace norm as $\tau\to\infty$ to $\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}=\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$, where $P_E$ is the spectral projection onto the full eigenspace of energy $E$. Coherences inside degenerate energy blocks remain. The limit need not be Gibbs, and no pointwise-in-time convergence or thermalization is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3.1 (printed pp. 18–19)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.3.1 and 4.4.1 (printed pp. 199–206)

items.physical_scope: A trace-class initial density and a self-adjoint quantum Hamiltonian with a complete discrete energy eigenfamily of finite multiplicity under the declared unitary dynamics; the result is a time-averaged state limit, not Gibbs preparation or pointwise relaxation.

items.title: Scope limits for finite ensembles, shells, pressure and dephasing
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
The finite canonical, maximum-entropy, independent-factorization and finite-bath claims concern the exact finite state spaces and shell-weight assumptions stated in their items. Countable and measurable derivative identities require their local summable or integrable moment envelopes; a lower energy bound alone does not normalize the partition function. The lattice bulk-pressure and concentration claims apply only to the bounded finite-range lattice model and, for concentration, a differentiability point of the limiting log-partition density. The page-level continuum-pressure prerequisite is a distinct interaction model; no stable-tempered continuum limit is inferred from the lattice theorem.

The classical shell result applies only to a nonempty compact regular level with the coarea normalization and a globally defined invertible flow on the stated band. It does not imply ergodicity or equality of long-time averages with the shell law. The quantum trace identities require a semibounded self-adjoint generator, a positive finite Gibbs trace and the stated moment envelope; discrete dephasing is a trace-norm Cesaro limit with degenerate eigenspaces retained, not pointwise relaxation or a Gibbs limit.

Boltzmann microstate entropy, finite Gibbs entropy, von Neumann entropy and the macroscopic entropy function are distinct objects until a model supplies an explicit identification. The statistical value $-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ is not silently identified with a macroscopic Helmholtz or grand potential. Canonical and microcanonical sampling are adopted preparation assumptions. None of the finite probability identities, continuum or lattice pressure limits, shell-invariance results or quantum trace calculations reports an experiment or establishes that nature follows the model.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.2–1.3 (printed pp. 2–27)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2–4.6 (printed pp. 192–217)

items.title: Identical bosonic modes do not have a finite infinite-mode Gibbs trace
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice as required by [[pthm-td-finite-mode-occupation-and-trace-formulas]] and the trace-class suppliers. Take modes indexed by $j\in\mathbb N$, each with excitation energy $\varepsilon>0$ joules, and let $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(0,1)$. Let $\mathcal F$ be the set of finite-support occupation sequences $n=(n_j)_{j\ge1}$ with $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$. Enumerate $\mathcal F$ by increasing $R(n)=\sum_{j:n_j>0}(j+n_j)$ and lexicographic order of the finite list of nonzero pairs $(j,n_j)$ within each level. Each level is finite because $j,n_j\le R(n)$ on its support, and every configuration occurs; skipping empty levels gives a bijection $\mathbb N\to\mathcal F$. Define
$$\ell^2(\mathcal F):=\Bigl\{c:\mathcal F\to\mathbb C:\sum_{n\in\mathcal F}|c(n)|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad \langle c,d\rangle:=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F}c(n)\overline{d(n)}.$$
The vector $|n\rangle$ is the indicator of $\{n\}$; these canonical occupation vectors form an orthonormal basis. Relabeling by the displayed enumeration is an isometry with $\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb C)$, which is a Hilbert space with its standard basis by [[ex-standard-basis-of-ell-two]]; the definition of square-summable families and their inner product is [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]. Define the bounded positive diagonal Gibbs weight $K_\beta|n\rangle=q^{\sum_jn_j}|n\rangle$. On the subspace with $n_j=0$ for every $j>M$, the corresponding finite-mode partition sum is the trace of that restriction.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§3.5–3.6
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§5.6–5.7

items.physical_scope: A countable family of independent identical bosonic modes at fixed positive excitation energy; the divergent positive trace rules out this particular normalized Gibbs density and says nothing about finite mode sets or renormalized models.

items.title: An identity dynamics leaves a noncanonical finite preparation unchanged
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement: Let $\Omega=\{a,b\}$ with energies $E_a=0$, $E_b=\varepsilon>0$ joules, and fix $T>0$ kelvins. The separately adopted canonical law has probabilities proportional to $(1,e^{-\beta\varepsilon})$. For the dynamical comparison, use a dimensionless model-time parameter $\tau\ge0$, stipulate the identity transition map $\Phi_\tau(a)=a$, $\Phi_\tau(b)=b$ for all $\tau$, and start with the point mass $\delta_a$.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4–4.6

items.physical_scope: A two-state finite model with explicitly frozen identity dynamics; it shows that a canonical preparation rule alone supplies no relaxation dynamics and is not an empirical statement.

items.title: Two isolated two-level sites do not relax an energy eigenstate to Gibbs form
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice for the canonical mode preparation. Let $\mathcal H_1=\mathcal H_2=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, and define the factor number maps by $N_r|0\rangle=0$, $N_r|1\rangle=|1\rangle$. The composite Hilbert space is the finite Hilbert tensor product $\mathcal H_1\widehat\otimes\mathcal H_2\cong\mathbb C^4$ from [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with orthonormal product basis $|n_1n_2\rangle$, $n_r\in\{0,1\}$. On this basis define the site-number operators $\mathcal N_1|n_1n_2\rangle=n_1|n_1n_2\rangle$ and $\mathcal N_2|n_1n_2\rangle=n_2|n_1n_2\rangle$. For $T>0$ kelvins set $\varepsilon=k_{\mathrm B}T\log2$ joules and define the noninteracting total Hamiltonian
$$H=\varepsilon(\mathcal N_1+\mathcal N_2),\qquad H|n_1n_2\rangle=\varepsilon(n_1+n_2)|n_1n_2\rangle.$$
The quantum Gibbs preparation at $T$ is used for the thermal comparison, and the closed-system unitary evolution is generated by $H$ with $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$, where $t$ is in seconds and $\hbar>0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Start the dynamics in $\rho_0=|00\rangle\langle00|$.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.1 and 3.6
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.3–4.4 and §5.7

items.physical_scope: A hypothetical closed two-site quantum model initialized in a product energy eigenstate; unitary evolution preserves that state and does not produce its finite-temperature Gibbs mixture. This is not an experiment.
